title: Progressive SLA/SLO & Release Gate Framework for Multi-tenant Embeddings and Low-latency Search
creator: Lina Gomez
description: Define concrete SLOs, error budgets, and step-wise release gates for the new multi-tenant embeddings + low-latency semantic search product. This ticket captures the PRD-level acceptance criteria, rollout safety checks, monitoring requirements, and cross-team dependencies required before we open the feature to paid tenants and Dedicated customers.
background: We introduced an embeddings inference path optimized for short-context semantic search queries (avg tokens/request ~ 32) and a multi-tenant routing layer for cost isolation. Performance gains were validated in lab with a mix of quantized models and CPU-offload kernels. Before broad rollout we need product-level SLOs, a clear error-budget-driven rollout plan, and operational runbook content to ensure predictable behavior in hosted and Dedicated modes.
goals: 1) Specify measurable availability and latency SLOs for both embeddings creation and the low-latency search route. 2) Define staged rollout gates tied to error budget consumption and staged tenant cohorts. 3) Provide acceptance criteria for e2e tests, contract tests, and monitoring dashboards. 4) Capture required alerts, runbooks and dependencies for Safe GA.
non_goals: 1) Redesign of the routing topology or kernel selection logic (handled by Runtime). 2) Changes to billing/price model. 3) Full Dedicated capacity reservation flows (separate PM ticket).
scope: Applies to hosted embeddings API (/v1/embeddings) and the low-latency search route (/v1/search/semantic) for single-turn requests. Covers SLO definitions, observability and rollout gates for tenant cohorts up to 100 tenants in staged release. Does not include batch embeddings pipelines or offline vector indexing jobs.
requirements: - Define SLO targets (p50/p95/p99) for latency per route and availability targets. - Define acceptable error types (5xx, timeouts, model-fallbacks) and how they decrement error budget. - Specify observability: required metrics, dashboards and synthetic probes. - Define automated rollback and throttling gates driven by burn rate. - Provide acceptance tests and CI contract checks used by CI and canary jobs.
sla_slo_definitions: Embeddings API (short queries): Availability: 99.9% monthly uptime. Latency SLOs: p50 <= 12ms, p95 <= 42ms, p99 <= 120ms (end-to-end server time measured from request arrival to first token emitted for embeddings). Error budget: 0.1% monthly allowable errors where errors = 5xx + timeouts + model-fallback-detected (fallbacks counted as degraded errors). Low-latency Search: Availability: 99.5% monthly. Latency SLOs: p50 <= 18ms, p95 <= 75ms, p99 <= 200ms (includes routing + KV cache lookup). For Dedicated customers: contractual SLA increases to availability 99.95% but only after capacity commit and runbook verification.
error_budget_and_burn_policy: Error budget tracked per-tenant and globally. Immediate alerts if 24h burn rate > 50% of remaining budget. Automated mitigation steps: 1) If tenant burn rate > 30% for 1 hour -> move tenant to degraded routing (cached model variant). 2) If global burn rate > 50% in 6 hours -> pause new tenant enrollments to staged cohort and trigger rollback candidate. 3) If monthly budget exhausted -> emergency throttle to read-only for non-critical tenants until next billing cycle or rollback.
rollout_gates: Stage 0 - Internal dogfood (0 tenants): verify synthetic probes and contract tests pass across regions. Entry condition: all critical alerts green for 48h. Stage 1 - Alpha (up to 10 friendly tenants): allow opt-in, limit QPS per tenant to 1rps. Entry condition: zero P1 incidents and p95 latency within 10% of target for 72h. Stage 2 - Beta (up to 50 tenants): increase QPS limits, enable production batching heuristics. Gate: cumulative error budget burn < 25% and burn-rate < 10%/day for 7 days. Stage 3 - Gradual GA (up to 100 tenants): enable full traffic but with per-tenant throttles. Gate: global error budget remaining >= 80% and monitoring alarms stable for 14 days. Final GA: open to all self-serve tenants after 30 days of Stage 3 and zero critical incidents; Dedicated onboarding requires runbook sign-off and load-run verification.
monitoring_and_alerting: Required metrics: per-route request rate, latency histograms (p50/p95/p99), 5xx count, timeout count, model-fallback count, cache-hit ratio, per-tenant error budget remaining. Dashboards: Embeddings SLO Overview (global + per-region), Tenant Burn Rate heatmap. Alerts: P1 if p99 exceeds target by >50% for 5m; P1 if 5xx spike >3x baseline for 2m; P2 if per-tenant burn rate >20% in 1h. Synthetic probes: global synthetic suite hitting each region every 1m with latency and correctness checks. Must create Grafana dashboards and Alertmanager rules before Stage 1.
operational_playbook: - On alert: run initial triage checklist (quickly identify if issue is model, runtime, or infra). - If model fallback count increases -> escalate to Applied ML and disable problematic model variant. - If cache-hit ratio drops unexpectedly -> run cache warmup and check routing policies. - Rollback criteria: sustained p95 > 2x SLO for >30min OR global error budget burn > 60% in 12h. - Post-incident: write incident report with root cause and runbook updates; update SLO if necessary.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Lab and canary traffic demonstrate p95 latency within 10% of target for 72h across regions. 2) Synthetic probes and contract tests created and passing in CI. 3) Dashboards and alerts live in Prod and testable. 4) Error-budget tracking implemented and visible per-tenant. 5) Runbook and rollback steps documented and reviewed by SRE and Applied ML. 6) Cross-functional sign-off from Runtime, SRE, Applied ML, and Security for Stage 1 entry.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Model-fallbacks increase error counts (mitigation: conservative initial model pairing and explicit fallback counting). Risk: Per-tenant noisy neighbors (mitigation: per-tenant throttles and burst isolation). Risk: Observability gaps (mitigation: require synthetic probes and contract tests before Stage 1). Risk: Unexpected cost rise due to traffic patterns (mitigation: telemetry on token-per-request and cost per 1k requests).
notes: We should surface per-tenant SLO opt-outs for experimental tenants with explicit consent. Review Dedicated SLA uplift with Legal before including in sales materials. Consider a follow-up ticket to define CI contract tests that intentionally inject model fallbacks to validate error counting.
